is_anopheles.evidence: Study evaluated field-caught Anopheles gambiae s.l. (predominantly An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii) in Faranah Prefecture, Guinea (Page 1, Abstract; Page 6, Results).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Paper genotyped L1014F kdr (Vgsc L995F), N1575Y (Vgsc N1570Y), and G119S Ace-1 (Ace-1 G280S) (Page 1, Abstract; Page 4-5, Methods; Tables 2 and 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts (RS, RR, SS) or sample sizes and frequencies are reported in text and tables: L1014F kdr (100% of 60 tested; Page 7), N1575Y counts by site/phenotype (Table 2, Page 9-10; 113/561 positive), and G119S Ace-1 counts by phenotype (Table 3, Page 11; 18/29 positive).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Balayani, Foulaya, Tindo, and Faranah city in Guinea between June 25th and July 20th, 2018 (Page 2, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical study reporting original field collections, bioassays, and molecular genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific villages and geographic coordinates provided: Balayani (10.1325, -10.7443), Foulaya (10.144633, -10.749717), Tindo (9.961223, -10.701656), and Faranah larvae site (10.042423, -10.740980) in Faranah Prefecture, Guinea (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected over a discrete period between June 25th and July 20th, 2018 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original field survey conducted in 2018 in Faranah, Guinea.

supplement.evidence: All primary genotype breakdown tables and bioassay results are fully contained in the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide susceptibility and resistance mechanisms in Anopheles gambiae s.l. from three villages and one larval site in Faranah Prefecture, Guinea in June-July 2018. High resistance to permethrin and deltamethrin and moderate resistance to bendiocarb were observed via CDC bottle bioassays. Genotyping revealed fixation of Vgsc L1014F (100%, 60/60), presence of Vgsc N1575Y (20%, 113/561), and Ace-1 G119S (62.1%, 18/29), with Ace-1 G119S strongly associated with bendiocarb survival. qRT-PCR also demonstrated metabolic overexpression of CYP6M2, CYP6P3, and GSTD3.
